newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam rice prices nudge lower as demand dries up.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam rice prices nudge lower as demand dries up.

text.p: Vietnam's rice export prices nudged lower this week as demand remained thin, but dealers said the market could pick up next month due to a delayed harvest in the Mekong Delta.
"There are just two vessels loading in Saigon at the moment," said one trader. "One's for Indonesia, the other is for Iran -- and they are both old contracts."

Traders put five percent broken grade, FOB Saigon Port, at $268-$270 a tonne compared with $275-$280 a week ago. Ten percent broken grade was also $7.0 lower at around $258 a tonne, while 25 percent was down about $3.0 at $242-$245.

There have been several contracts already sealed for the first quarter, including a shipment of 60,000 tonnes to Iraq as part of a United Nations-approved oil-for- food deal. Traders said state-owned Vinafood would supply 30,000 tonnes and the rest would come from private traders.
There was talk of a new deal to supply rice to the Philippines, but there were still no details of the amount that might be shipped or a delivery period.

The Vietnam Economic Times said domestic prices had moved higher because the southern ricebowl's spring crop would be delayed by recent heavy flooding. Traders said harvesting, which usually starts in February and continues until April, may be a month late.
